evals.name: tabular-clinical-interpretability
evals.prompt: I've got a csv of patient data at D:\projects\TsetlinMachineSkill\tsetlin-machine-workspace\inputs\patients.csv - 30 numeric columns, 500 rows, binary outcome in the readmitted_30d column. A colleague said tsetlin machines are the thing when you need to actually explain the model to a clinician. Can you write me something that works?
evals.expected_output: A runnable script that booleanizes the continuous columns explicitly, trains a pyTsetlinMachine MultiClassTsetlinMachine (correct positional constructor), reports held-out accuracy against the majority-class baseline, and prints the learned clauses translated back into the user's real column names. T and s stated as starting points. Hidden ground truth in the data: (hba1c > 8.0 AND age > 65) OR (n_prior_admissions >= 3) OR (egfr < 45 AND albumin < 3.4), with 8% label noise, 23.8% positive rate.
assertions: Uses a real Tsetlin Machine library with the correct constructor signature (pyTsetlinMachine MultiClassTsetlinMachine(clauses, T, s) positionally, or TMU TMClassifier with keyword args) rather than an invented or hallucinated API
Booleanizes the continuous columns explicitly with a named method (Binarizer, thresholding, thermometer encoding) instead of feeding raw floats to the TM
Prints or states the feature count before and after booleanization, so the user can see how many Boolean features resulted
Holds out a test set and reports test accuracy, not training accuracy
Reports the majority-class baseline (~76%) or another comparison, so accuracy on this imbalanced outcome is not read as impressive on its own
Prints the learned clauses, not only accuracy - the script delivers interpretability rather than just a score
Translates clause literals back into the user's real column names and threshold values (e.g. 'hba1c > 8.0'), not raw literal indices like 'feature 147'
Handles negated literals correctly, using the n_features offset to distinguish x_k from NOT x_k
States T and s as starting points to be tuned, with a suggested search range, rather than presenting single silently-chosen values as final
Excludes the patient_id column from the model features
Is honest about what was actually run: if the library did not install, says so rather than reporting accuracy figures it never measured

The delivered clause output recovers at least one of the hidden ground-truth conditions (hba1c high AND age high; n_prior_admissions >= 3; egfr low AND albumin low), or the script is structured so it would surface them when run
